title: O Light That Knew No Dawn
description: O Light That Knew No Dawn in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900), headed “St. Gregory”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), and this page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Light that knew no dawn, That shines to end-less day, All things in earth and heaven Are lus-tred by Thy ray; No eye can to Thy throne as-cend, Nor mind Thy bright-ness com-pre-hend.

lines: O Light that knew no dawn,
That shines to endless day,
All things in earth and heaven
Are lustred by Thy ray;
No eye can to Thy throne ascend,
Nor mind Thy brightness comprehend.
Thy grace, O Father, give,
That I may serve in fear;
Above all boons, I pray,
Grant me Thy voice to hear;
From sin Thy child in mercy free,
And let me dwell in light with Thee.
That, cleansed from filthy stain,
I may meet homage give,
And, pure in heart, behold
And serve Thee while I live;
Clean hands in holy worship raise,
And Thee, O Christ my Saviour, praise.
In supplication meek
To Thee I bend the knee;
O Christ, when Thou shalt come,
In love remember me,
And in Thy kingdom, by Thy grace,
Grant me a humble servant's place.
Thy grace, O Father, give,
I humbly Thee implore;
And let Thy mercy bless
Thy servant more and more.
All grace and glory be to Thee
From age to age eternally.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
